subject: NeuroScale bridge-rate smoothing / onboarding concession request
messages:
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@neuroscale.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on proposal + onramp smoothing

Irene —

Thanks for the proposal. The team is excited about Redwood but we have a narrow pilot budget and a clinical timeline that forces a faster ramp than your standard rate ladder. Two asks from our side:

1) Can Redwood provide a transient onboarding concession for the first 6 months (we were thinking ~40% off list for the pilot window) to help us get to 100k daily tokens without triggering a full-tier commitment?
2) Could you smooth the tier breakpoints so we don't jump 2 pricing tiers when usage hits the spike (happens during our nightly batch jobs)?

Attached is an updated SOW and expected token profile. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Tan
Head of ML Ops, NeuroScale Health
[Attachment: SOW-NeuroScale-v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Questions on proposal + onramp smoothing

Team — forwarding NeuroScale's ask. Summary: they want a 6-month onboarding concession and smoother tier breakpoints to avoid big price jumps during nightly batch spikes. SOW attached. Key constraints: they're strategic in cardiac/neurology space (potential for broader rollout) but current budget only supports a fragile pilot.

Proposed internal posture (my recommendation): 35% one-time onboarding credit applied as a rebate (not rate change) for first 6 months, with a hard cap (to protect unit economics) and a 12-month minimum rollback if they convert — we should tie it to an ARR commitment or auto-reversion to list rates. This would be an exception to our standard onramp policy and will need VP/CFO sign-off.

Questions for approvals:
- Karthik: acceptable concession level and exec memo wording?
- Marissa: can you run the revenue impact and suggest a dollar cap we can commit to?
- Jordan: any legal/commercial guardrails we should insist on (audit rights, termination if abuse)?

Attachments: SOW-NeuroScale-v2.pdf, redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx (attached)

Thanks — need quick turn, they want to close terms this week.

—Irene
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on proposal + onramp smoothing

Irene — thanks for the summary. A few quick points:

1) 35% is a big delta vs standard starter credits; I don't want to default to that without a clear mitigation for revenue erosion. If we're leaning that way, tie the concession to a minimum 12-month commitment at a measured ARR (or a minimum dollar spend) plus a clawback if they churn under X months.

2) Alternative: 25% onboarding credit + a smoothing policy (temporary effective tier smoothing that automatically reverts after 6 months). That reduces downside and preserves list rates for long-term usage.

3) We should cap the total onboarding credit (dollar limit) — ask Marissa to model throughput scenarios (low/expected/high) and give me a recommended cap and expected hit to Q3/Q4 revenue.

4) Jordan — please flag any contractual language you need for audit/usage verification and an explicit carveout if we detect systematic batch manipulation as described.

I'll draft a one-page exec memo for VP/CFO sign-off once Marissa gives numbers. Time is tight; if we miss this week the prospect shifts to an alternative provider.

-Karthik
VP Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on proposal + onramp smoothing

Adding the numbers from a quick run of the onboarding credit model (attached onboarding-credit-model.csv):

- Expected 6-month incremental token consumption: 18M tokens (pilot central estimate)
- If we provide a 35% unit discount for 6 months (no cap): estimated revenue hit = ~$92k (accrual impact Q3/Q4).
- If we cap the credit at $45k (one-time rebate): effective average concession ~27% for expected usage, downside protected at high-usage scenario.
- 25% unconditional credit + smoothing policy: estimated hit = ~$62k; lower downside but may not be sufficient to close.

Recommendation: Approve a one-time onboarding rebate capped at $45k, applied as a credit on invoices over the first 6 months. Require a 12-month minimum contract term at a $200k ARR floor or a 6-month clawback if they terminate before 12 months.

I've attached the pricing matrix and the model for review. If leadership wants a deeper sensitivity, I can run the workbook this afternoon.

—Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations
[Attachment: onboarding-credit-model.csv (csv)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on proposal + onramp smoothing

Irene / all — legal/commercial notes:

- We should document the onboarding concession as an appendix (one-off credit schedule) rather than altering published list rates. That keeps our catalog intact.
- Require rights to audit usage for 12 months post-signing and explicit definitions of "batch spike" vs normal traffic. If their nightly jobs are legitimate and consistent, smoothing should be scheduled into operational SLAs.
- Recommend a termination/clawback clause: if they cancel within 6 months, the unused portion of the credit is recouped as invoice.
- I can prepare the appendix language; advise if you want to preserve any special termination language for clinical trial caveats.

Also suggest we assign the HubSpot deal ID (added link) and get finance to hardbook the $45k cap as a potential reduction to recognized revenue.

—Jordan
Senior Commercial Counsel

Karthik / VP Finance / CFO —

Summary: NeuroScale requests a 6-month onboarding concession to smooth their early ramp. RevOps recommends a one-time onboarding rebate capped at $45k (applied across invoices in months 1–6). Conditions: a 12-month minimum contract or 6-month clawback, audit rights for 12 months, and appendix language prepared by Legal.

Why approve: NeuroScale is a strategically valuable prospect in cardiac imaging; the pilot is time-sensitive and likely to convert to multi-region usage if we win the evaluation. The $45k cap balances closing chance vs revenue protection and is within the deal-level exceptions we have approved historically for strategic pilots.

Request: VP/CFO sign-off for the exception and authorization to include the rebate appendix and smoothing schedule in the SOW. If approved, Jordan will finalize wording and Marissa will apply the cap in the billing system.

If you approve, please reply-all with an explicit sign-off and any amendments. Alex, copying you so you have the final pathway.

Thanks —
Irene
Director, Strategic Accounts
